brief: A podcast player where episodes are constellations — listened ones glow, series form patterns

dominant_strengths: Evocative metaphor — listened/unlistened states map cleanly to glowing vs dim stars, reinforcing the constellation concept
Restrained palette of cyan, amber, and deep purple creates a genuine cosmic mood without kitsch
Tracked-out small caps labels feel astronomical-chart appropriate, pairing well with the airy serif-less title
dominant_weaknesses: Zero podcast-player affordances visible — no play state, episode title, scrubber, or queue, so the brief is half-built
Constellations float in arbitrary positions with weak spatial logic; categories don't read as a navigable system
Connecting lines between stars are almost invisible, undercutting the 'series form patterns' promise
fix_priorities: Add a persistent now-playing surface and hover/selected episode metadata to make it a player not a poster
Strengthen constellation linework and give each cluster a distinct shape that reads as a series identity
Establish a clearer compositional grid or orbit so categories relate rather than scatter
Introduce subtle parallax/twinkle motion cues to signal interactivity
rationale.norman_balance: Strong visceral and reflective pull from the cosmic metaphor, but behavioral utility is severely underdeveloped — you can admire it but not operate it.
rationale.intent_fit: Captures the poetic half of the brief beautifully yet fails the 'player' half, leaving it closer to a concept illustration than a functional podcast interface.
